paper.title: Reflexion: reinforcement via verbal reflection
paper.task: An LLM agent (the Actor) acts in an environment over repeated trials; an Evaluator scores each trajectory, a Self-Reflection model turns the trajectory and its reward into verbal feedback stored in memory, and the Actor uses that memory in later trials until the Evaluator deems the trajectory correct.

components.name: Environment
components.what: the task environment the Actor interacts with; returns observations o_t to the Actor's actions a_t

provenance.quote: we sample an action or generation, a t , from the current policy π θ at time t, receive an observation from the environment o t

components.name: Actor
components.what: M_a: an LLM prompted to generate text and actions (policy π_θ) conditioned on state observations and memory; variants explored include Chain of Thought and ReAct

provenance.quote: The Actor is built upon a large language model (LLM) that is specifically prompted to generate the necessary text and actions conditioned on the state observations

components.name: Evaluator
components.what: M_e: takes a generated trajectory and computes a reward score; variants are exact-match (EM) grading, pre-defined heuristic functions, or an LLM used as Evaluator

provenance.quote: It takes as input a generated trajectory and computes a reward score that reflects its performance within the given task context

components.name: Self-Reflection
components.what: M_sr: an LLM that, given the sparse reward, the current trajectory and memory mem, generates verbal self-reflection feedback sr_t for future trials

provenance.quote: The Self-Reflection model instantiated as an LLM, plays a crucial role in the Reflexion framework by generating verbal self-reflections to provide valuable feedback for future trials

components.name: Memory
components.what: the agent's memory, made of a short-term and a long-term memory that together provide context to the Actor

provenance.quote: Core components of the Reflexion process are the notion of short-term and long-term memory
In the RL setup, the trajectory history serves as the short-term memory

components.name: Long-term memory (mem)
components.what: stores the Self-Reflection outputs sr_t (each appended after trial t); bounded to a maximum of Ω stored experiences (usually 1-3)

contributions.text: Reflexion: reinforcement via verbal reflection - a Self-Reflection model generates verbal reinforcement cues that help the Actor self-improve

provenance.quote: a Self-Reflection model, denoted as M sr , which generates verbal reinforcement cues to assist the Actor in self-improvement

contributions.text: short-term (trajectory) and long-term (self-reflection) memory working together, claimed as a key advantage of Reflexion agents over other LLM action-choice works

provenance.quote: These two memory components work together to provide context that is specific but also influenced by lessons learned over several trials, which is a key advantage of Reflexion agents over other LLM action choice works

contributions.text: Reflexion formalized as an iterative optimization process over trials (trial, evaluation, self-reflection, memory update)

provenance.quote: Reflexion is formalized as an iterative optimization process

unclear: The text never states outright that mem is the long-term memory; it says Self-Reflection outputs are stored in mem and also that they are stored in long-term memory, so long_term_mem is named 'Long-term memory (mem)'. The early sentence 'we also add a memory component mem that provides additional context to this agent' could also cover both memories.

Novelty: the text has no explicit contribution list. The Actor (an LLM with CoT/ReAct variants) and the Evaluator (EM grading, heuristics, or an LLM) are marked reused, the weaker role; only the Self-Reflection model and the memory are marked proposed.
Where the Self-Reflection model's 'current trajectory' comes from (the Actor directly, or the short-term memory) is not stated; it is drawn from the Actor.
That the Actor writes its trajectory into short-term memory is inferred from 'the trajectory history serves as the short-term memory'; no explicit write step is described.

The Evaluator's reward is not stated to reach the Actor directly; only its role in stopping the loop ('until the Evaluator deems τ t to be correct') is stated, recorded as a control edge evaluator -> actor.
The final output when the loop stops is not described.
'formalized as an iterative optimization process in 1' and 'As mentioned in 3' refer to an algorithm/section not included in the text.
The equation 'r t = M e (τ 0 )' mixes indices t and 0 in the text; read as r_t = M_e(τ_t).
Whether the policy parameters θ are ever updated is not stated.
